turns.content:
Build a multi-page website for "Artisan Goods Co.",
a handmade crafts shop. I need:
- Homepage with a hero banner, featured products
  section, and a newsletter signup
- Product catalog page with category filters
  (pottery, textiles, woodwork, jewelry) and a grid
  of product cards with images, names, and prices
- About page with our story, team member profiles
  with photos, and a mission statement
- Shared navigation header and footer across all
  pages
Use React Router for page navigation. Products
should be fetched from an API endpoint.

I'll build the Artisan Goods Co. website systematically. Let me start with Phase 1 — all setup tasks in parallel.Colors and fonts are set. Now let me fetch all the images and create the API endpoint in parallel.All images fetched. Now generating the logo and creating the API endpoint simultaneously.Logo generated. Now let me register the API route and read the existing server entry and routes files to update them.API registered. Now let me verify it works, then build the Header and Footer in parallel.API is live. Now building the Header and Footer:Now building all three pages. Let me start with the shared ProductCard component and then build all pages in parallel.Now building all three pages simultaneously:Now update routes.tsx to wire up all three pages with their loaders:Now let me also update the RootLayout to ensure the site-wide SEO defaults are set:All 5 tasks complete. Let me do a quick check to make sure the API endpoints work correctly:Everything is working perfectly. Let me show the completed todo list:The Artisan Goods Co. website is fully built — all 5 tasks complete. Here's what was delivered:

- **Homepage** — full-bleed hero with animated headline, 4 featured products fetched from the API, a values strip, and an asymmetric newsletter signup with a decorative image
- **Product Catalog** (`/products`) — sticky category filter bar (All / Pottery / Textiles / Woodwork / Jewelry), 12-product grid with staggered fade-in animations, and URL-based filtering
- **About Page** (`/about`) — atmospheric hero, pull-quote mission statement, two-column brand story with decorative offset image, and team profiles with photos
- **Header** — sticky with scroll shadow, logo, nav links with animated underlines, "Shop Now" CTA, and mobile hamburger menu
- **Footer** — dark walnut background, 4-column layout (brand, links, categories, newsletter), social icons
- **Products API** — `/api/products` with `?category=` and `?featured=true` filtering, 12 products across all 4 categories

input.prompt:
Build a multi-page artisan crafts website with this design direction:

PROJECT DETAILS:
- Business: Artisan Goods Co. — handmade crafts shop
- Categories: Pottery, Textiles, Woodwork, Jewelry
- Pages: Homepage, Product Catalog, About

DESIGN DIRECTION:
Warm, earthy, handcrafted aesthetic that feels like stepping into a boutique maker's market. Organic textures, generous whitespace, and editorial typography that honors the handmade nature of the products. NOT a generic e-commerce template — this should feel curated and artisanal.

LAYOUT TYPE: Standard
Multi-page site with full navigation header and footer.

VISUAL DIRECTION:
- Color: Warm neutrals — cream/off-white base, warm terracotta accent, deep walnut brown for text. Avoid pure white or cold grays.
- Typography: Serif display font for headings (warmth, craft heritage), clean sans-serif for body. Mix weights confidently — oversized hero headline.
- Layout: Full-bleed hero with editorial feel. Product grid with generous spacing. NO uniform icon grids.

VISUAL ELEMENTS:
- Primary: Photography — artisan product photos with natural lighting, warm tones
- Style: Authentic handmade product shots, close-up textures, natural materials
- Application: Hero uses a full-bleed craft/product image; product cards use individual product photos; team section uses portrait photos
- Logo: Wordmark-style logo with a subtle craft/leaf/hand icon. Use media-logo skill to generate.

MOTION DESIGN:
- Level: Subtle
- Effects: Fade-in on scroll for product cards (staggered, 300ms), gentle hover lift on product cards (translate-y -4px + shadow), smooth underline hover on nav links
- Personality: Warm and unhurried — nothing fast or jarring

SECTION-SPECIFIC:

Hero (Homepage):
- Full-bleed background image of artisan workspace or beautiful handmade goods
- Oversized serif headline ("Handcrafted with Heart") left-aligned
- Short tagline and two CTAs: "Shop Now" → /products, "Our Story" → /about
- Subtle fade-in entrance animation

Featured Products (Homepage):
- Section title: "Featured Pieces"
- Show 4 featured products in a 2x2 or 4-column grid
- Each card: product image, name, category badge, price
- Hover lift effect on cards
- "View All" link to /products

Newsletter Signup (Homepage):
- Warm, integrated section (NOT a generic colored band)
- Asymmetric layout with decorative element
- Email input + "Subscribe" button
- Copy: "Join our community of craft lovers"

Product Catalog (/products):
- Category filter bar at top: All | Pottery | Textiles | Woodwork | Jewelry
- Active filter highlighted with terracotta accent
- Product grid: responsive 2-col mobile, 3-col tablet, 4-col desktop
- Each card: image, name, category, price
- Products fetched from /api/products (with optional ?category= query param)
- Staggered fade-in as products load

About Page (/about):
- Hero section: brand story headline + atmospheric image
- Mission statement in large, elegant typography (pull-quote style)
- "Our Story" narrative section (2-col: text left, image right)
- Team profiles: 3-column grid, each with photo, name, role, short bio
- Warm, editorial feel throughout

Header:
- Logo left, nav links right: Home | Shop | About
- Clean, minimal — warm background (cream/off-white), not stark white
- Sticky on scroll with subtle shadow
- Mobile hamburger menu

Footer:
- Multi-column: Brand blurb | Quick Links | Categories | Newsletter teaser
- Warm dark background (walnut brown), cream text
- Social icons
- Copyright line

DIFFERENTIATION:
Oversized serif headline in the hero that breaks the grid. Product cards with warm cream backgrounds (not white) and terracotta category badges. The newsletter section uses an asymmetric layout with a decorative botanical/craft motif.

CONSISTENCY:
Maintain warm, artisanal energy throughout all pages and sections. Footer should feel as intentional as the hero. Terracotta accent used consistently for CTAs, active states, and badges.

BUILD ORDER:

Phase 1 — Setup (run in parallel):
- Search for images: artisan workspace hero, pottery products, textile products, woodwork products, jewelry products, team portrait photos (3), about page atmospheric image
- Set font stack using fontTheme tool: serif display (e.g. Playfair Display or Lora) + clean sans (e.g. Inter or DM Sans)
- Set color scheme using colorTheme tool: cream background, terracotta primary, walnut brown foreground
- Create the Products API endpoint at src/server/api/products.ts with mock product data (12+ products across 4 categories: pottery, textiles, woodwork, jewelry). Each product: id, name, category, price, description, imageUrl, featured (boolean). Register it in src/server/entry.ts at GET /api/products (supports ?category= filter and returns featured products if ?featured=true).

Phase 2 — Structure (run in parallel, after Phase 1):
- Build Header (src/layouts/parts/Header.tsx): sticky, cream background, logo left, nav right (Home/Shop/About), mobile menu
- Build Footer (src/layouts/parts/Footer.tsx): dark walnut background, multi-column layout, social icons, copyright

Phase 3 — Pages (after Phase 1 & 2):
- Add routes to src/routes.tsx: / (Homepage), /products (Catalog), /about (About)
- Build Homepage (src/pages/index.tsx): hero, featured products (fetched from /api/products?featured=true via loader), newsletter signup
- Build Product Catalog (src/pages/products.tsx): category filters, product grid (fetched from /api/products via loader, supports category filtering client-side)
- Build About page (src/pages/about.tsx): story, mission statement, team profiles

Phase 4 — Finalize:
- Mark all todo items as COMPLETE using the todoList tool
- Ask for design feedback using askQuestion

CRITICAL: Build pages LAST — after setup, API, header, and footer are done.

TODO LIST IDs (mark complete after finishing each):
- Homepage: 1780031907165-s5k9358
- Product catalog page: 1780031907165-ebxhd1i
- About page: 1780031907165-9btegk4
- Products API endpoint: 1780031907165-xlwowww
- Shared header & footer: 1780031907165-1j2ufuw
List ID: 1780031907165-qphz6mh

DESIGN FEEDBACK:
After showing the site, use askQuestion tool to ask:
- Question: "What do you think of the design?"
- Suggestions: ["Looks great — it's done!", "Adjust the color scheme", "Change the fonts", "Tweak the product card layout", "Update the homepage hero"]

Our Story

A Studio, a Vision, a Community

Artisan Goods Co. began in 2018 in a small backyard pottery studio in Portland, Oregon. Founder Elena Vasquez had grown tired of mass-produced goods that felt disposable — objects with no story, no soul.

She started inviting other makers — weavers, woodworkers, jewelers — to share their work through a single curated platform. The idea was simple: connect people who make things with care to people who appreciate that care.

Today, we work with over 40 independent artisans across North America, each vetted for their craft, their ethics, and their commitment to making things that last. Every piece in our collection is made by hand, in small batches, with materials that are honest and natural.

turns.content: I want to make sure the product catalog page is actually pulling data from a service module or API call in the component code — not just listing products as hardcoded arrays in the JSX. Can you check how the products page is loading its data and make sure it's fetching from the `/api/products` endpoint through a proper service layer or data fetching function, not inline hardcoded product objects in the component markup?

Let me check the current state of the products page and related files.The products page is already doing the right thing — it's fetching from `/api/products` via a route `loader` function (lines 6–11), and the component reads that data through `useLoaderData()` (line 22). There are no hardcoded product arrays in the component at all.

That said, your instinct about a proper service layer is a good one. Right now the `fetch` call lives directly in the loader. Let me extract it into a dedicated `src/lib/products-api.ts` service module so the data-fetching logic is centralized and reusable:Now update both pages to import from the service module instead of calling `fetch` inline:Now update `ProductCard` to import `Product` from the service module rather than defining its own copy:Good. Now let me verify the API still responds correctly end-to-end:All good. Here's a summary of what the data flow looks like now:

**`src/lib/products-api.ts`** — the single source of truth for all product fetching. Exports `productsApi.getAll()`, `productsApi.getFeatured()`, and `productsApi.getByCategory()`, each building the correct query string and calling `/api/products`.

**`src/pages/products.tsx`** — its `loader` calls `productsApi.getAll()`. The component reads the result via `useLoaderData()` and filters client-side by the active category tab. No product data is hardcoded anywhere in the JSX.

**`src/pages/index.tsx`** — its `loader` calls `productsApi.getFeatured()`. Same pattern.

The `Product` type is now defined once in `products-api.ts` and re-exported from `ProductCard.tsx` for backward compatibility — no duplicate interface definitions.

Can you confirm that all three pages (homepage, products, and about) are getting the header and footer from one reusable layout component, rather than each page importing and rendering Header and Footer on its own?

Let me check the relevant files to confirm the layout architecture.Confirmed — the architecture is exactly right. Here's how it works:

- **`RootLayout.tsx`** is the single shared component that renders `<Header />`, `{children}`, and `<Footer />` in one place (lines 33–35). Neither `Header` nor `Footer` is imported anywhere else.
- **`App.tsx`** wraps the entire route tree in `<RootLayout><Outlet /></RootLayout>` (lines 30–33, 41–50). `<Outlet />` is where React Router injects whichever page matches the current URL — so every route automatically gets the header and footer without doing anything themselves.
- **The grep confirms** that none of the three page files (`index.tsx`, `products.tsx`, `about.tsx`) import `Header` or `Footer` at all.

The flow is: `App.tsx` → `RootLayout` (header + footer) → `Outlet` → individual page component. Each page only renders its own content section — the shared chrome is handled entirely by the layout above it.
